mainTopic: A father naming one heir to inherit everything: the dispute of the תנא קמא and רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the הלכה, and its source in the פסוק.
overview: This amud opens with the last word of the previous discussion, then starts a new משנה. The משנה rules that a man who names someone below the Torah's heir, like another person when he has a daughter or a daughter when he has a son, has said nothing. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that naming someone fit to inherit him works. The גמרא infers that the first opinion also allows one son among sons, so the two opinions seem identical. A suggestion that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה goes further is pushed back by a ברייתא from his son רבי ישמעאל. The גמרא then gives two answers: either the משנה follows the first speaker of that ברייתא, or the whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה with missing words. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and רבא finds his source in 'ביום הנחילו את בניו'. אביי objects that 'לא יוכל לבכר' already teaches this. The גמרא answers that this phrase is needed for a ברייתא of אבא חנן, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The last item of the previous list: betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends with the word 'and betrothal,' the final item in a list of exceptions.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes the earlier discussion before the new משנה begins. It is the last item on a list of cases where taking back your words right away does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, saying something and quickly taking it back (תוך כדי דיבור) cancels what was said. קידושין is listed as an exception: once a man betroths a woman, a quick retraction does not undo it.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
Within the time it takes to speak a short greeting; the window in which you can usually take back your words

phrases.english: And betrothal.
phrases.notes: This finishes a list from the previous page: cases where quickly taking back your words doesn't work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the previous sugya before the new משנה begins.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קידושין, like the other items on the list, cannot be undone by a quick retraction.

steps.title: The משנה: you cannot change the Torah's heir
steps.stepSummary: A man who says an outsider will inherit him when he has a daughter, or that his daughter will inherit him when he has a son, has said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a man says 'So-and-so will inherit me' when he has a daughter, or 'My daughter will inherit me' when he has a son, his words mean nothing. He made a condition against what is written in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The new משנה gives the first opinion, the תנא קמא. You cannot move the inheritance away from the heir the Torah chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה sets an order: a son comes before a daughter, and a daughter comes before more distant relatives or outsiders. Trying to skip over the rightful heir is a תנאי against the תורה, so it is void.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
He will inherit me
He has said nothing; his words have no effect
He made a condition against what is written in the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: This is about inheritance (ירושה), which happens after death. It is not about giving a gift (מתנה) while alive. A father can still give his property away as a gift.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who says: "So-and-so will inherit me"
in a case where there is a daughter;
or "My daughter will inherit me" where there is a son –
he has said nothing,
since he stipulated against what is written in the Torah.
phrases.notes: The תורה's order of who inherits is in במדבר 27.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Naming as heir someone the Torah ranks below the actual heir has no effect.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: naming someone fit to inherit works
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that naming someone fit to inherit him works, but naming someone not fit to inherit does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: if he said it about someone fit to inherit him, his words stand. If he said it about someone not fit to inherit him, his words do not stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. It divides cases by whether the named person is 'fit to inherit' the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, the key question is whether the person is someone who could be an heir at all. The משנה does not explain how far 'fit to inherit' reaches, and that question is what the גמרא will now explore.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit to inherit him; someone who belongs among his possible heirs
His words stand; they take effect

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר עַל מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: if he said it about one fit to inherit him –
his words stand;

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מִי שֶׁאֵין רָאוּי לוֹ לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: but about one who is not fit to inherit him –
his words do not stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second opinion in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Designating an heir works if he is fit to inherit and fails if he is not.

steps.title: Inference: one son among sons does work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the first opinion closely and infers that naming one son among sons, or one daughter among daughters, does take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The reason his words fail is that he named an outsider in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son. But one son among the sons, or one daughter among the daughters, his words stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a דיוק from the cases the תנא קמא chose to mention. It is setting up a problem with the next opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא only said the words fail when the heir is skipped over completely. That implies that picking one of several equal heirs (one son among sons) is allowed. In that case he is not overriding the Torah, just choosing among people who already inherit.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
The reason is; the opener of an inference
But this; it follows that
One son among the sons

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The reason is that it was another in place of a daughter,
or a daughter in place of a son;
but a son among the sons,
or a daughter among the daughters –
his words stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied ruling from the תנא קמא's wording in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, choosing one heir among equal heirs is valid.

steps.title: Then רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is saying the same thing
steps.stepSummary: If the תנא קמא already agrees that one son among sons works, then רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule about someone 'fit to inherit' seems identical to his.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says that if he said it about someone fit to inherit him, his words stand. That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Where do the two opinions actually disagree?
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the inference in step 4, both opinions seem to say that naming someone who already inherits works. A משנה would not present two opinions as a dispute if they say the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the latter clause; look at the end of the משנה
This is the same as the first תנא

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר עַל מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: if he said it about one fit to inherit him –
his words stand.
This is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 4 to attack the need for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's presentation of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה as disagreeing with the תנא קמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both allow naming one heir among equals, there is no dispute left between them.

steps.title: Suggestion: he allows even a daughter in place of a son
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה goes further and allows even an outsider in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה means that even another relative in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son, works...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to find the dispute. It is only a suggestion, and the next step will challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe 'fit to inherit' is broad. A daughter, or a relative further down the line, could someday inherit if the closer heirs were gone, so they count as fit even now. If so, he disagrees with the תנא קמא about exactly the cases the משנה listed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say; introduces a suggested answer
He is saying

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. The phrase וכי תימא signals an idea that is about to be rejected.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה –
phrases.english: And if you would say that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka –
even another in place of a daughter
and a daughter in place of a son, he is saying;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the challenge of step 5 by widening the meaning of 'fit to inherit.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the scope of one opinion
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה allows even someone further down the line, which the תנא קמא forbids.

steps.title: His own son says they agree in those cases
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. He says his father and the חכמים did not argue about an outsider in place of a daughter or a daughter in place of a son: in those cases the words mean nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says: My father and the חכמים did not disagree about an outsider in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son. In those cases he has said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 6 using a ברייתא. The dispute cannot be about the cases the תנא קמא listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל reports his father's view, and he says his father agrees in exactly these cases. So the suggestion in step 6 fails, and the question from step 5 (where do they disagree?) comes back. Steps 9 and 10 answer it.

keyTerms.meaning: They did not disagree
My father
The Sages who disagree with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה in this ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: Once these cases are ruled out, the גמרא will have to find a different case where the two opinions really differ.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka, says:
My father and the Rabbis did not disagree
about another in place of a daughter
or a daughter in place of a son,
that he has said nothing;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer of step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה allows an outsider in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His own son testifies that in those cases his father agrees with the חכמים that the words are void.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: the real argument is about one son among sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל finishes his ברייתא. The real dispute is about one son among sons, or one daughter among daughters. His father says that heir inherits everything, and the חכמים say he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what did they argue about? About one son among the sons, or one daughter among the daughters. My father says that child inherits everything, and the חכמים say he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא. He says the true argument is about choosing one son among sons, or one daughter among daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the ברייתא (Step 7) knocked out the answer from Step 6, because outsider cases are not argued about at all. This second half makes things harder. The חכמים say even one son among sons does NOT work, but in Step 4 the גמרא read the משנה's first opinion as agreeing that it does work.

keyTerms.meaning: About what did they argue?
One son chosen from among several sons
My father (here, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה)
He will inherit (the whole estate)

steps.confusionAlert: In this ברייתא the חכמים say one son among sons does NOT work. Yet in Step 4 we read the משנה's first opinion as saying it DOES work. Keep these two readings apart. That clash is exactly what the next steps deal with.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About a son among the sons,
and a daughter among the daughters;
for my father says: he inherits [everything],
and the Rabbis say: he does not inherit [everything]!

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ – עַל בֵּן בֵּין הַבָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 7 and names the real case of the dispute.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects Step 6's answer. It also clashes with Step 4's reading that the first opinion lets one son among sons inherit.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רבי ישמעאל, nobody argues about outsiders. The only dispute is about one son among sons, and there the חכמים say it does not work.

steps.title: First answer: the opening voice of the ברייתא held they did argue
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל says 'they did not argue.' That shows the first voice in the ברייתא held that they DID argue about outsider cases. The משנה follows that first voice, so Step 6's answer can stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you like, say: since רבי ישמעאל says 'they did not argue,' the first speaker in the ברייתא must have held that they did argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first way out. רבי ישמעאל was answering someone, and that earlier opinion said there was an argument even about outsider cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'they did not argue' only make sense as a reply to someone who said they did. So there was an earlier opinion in which רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה even lets another relative who could someday inherit replace a daughter, or a daughter replace a son. The משנה can follow that view, and then רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה does add something new beyond the first opinion of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say this (introduces a possible answer)
From the fact that he says
It follows that / we can infer
Holds, is of the opinion

phrases.english: If you want, say:
from the fact that he says 'they did not disagree'
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי ישמעאל, in the ברייתא from Step 7.

phrases.english: it follows that the first Tanna holds: they did disagree.
phrases.notes: This means the first speaker in the ברייתא, not the first opinion in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Saves Step 6's answer from the ברייתא of Steps 7–8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits between the speakers in the ברייתא: the משנה follows the first speaker, not רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל's ברייתא shows that no one ever let an outsider replace a daughter, so Step 6 fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first speaker in the ברייתא held there was a dispute even about outsider cases. The משנה can follow him, so רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה does go beyond the first opinion.

steps.title: Second answer: the whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, with missing words
steps.stepSummary: Another way out: the whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view, and some words are missing. Read it this way: an outsider in place of a daughter, or a daughter in place of a son, means nothing. But one son among sons, or one daughter among daughters, does work, because he allows anyone fit to inherit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you like, say the whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and words are missing. It teaches: if someone says 'So-and-so will inherit me' when he has a daughter, or 'My daughter will inherit me' when he has a son, his words mean nothing. But for a daughter among daughters or a son among sons, if he said 'he inherits all my property,' his words stand. This is because רבי יוחנן says that naming someone fit to inherit works.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. The two parts of the משנה are not two different opinions at all. They are one opinion, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's, once we fill in the missing words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no 'first opinion' that repeats רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, so the question from Step 5 goes away. The first part tells us which cases fail: outsider for a daughter, daughter for a son. The second part gives his reason: anyone fit to inherit, like one son among sons, works. This also fits רבי ישמעאל's report that the חכמים disagree about one son among sons, because the חכמים simply are not in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole thing
Something is missing (from the wording)
And this is what it teaches
He has said nothing; his words have no effect
His words stand, they take effect

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to 'Isn't רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה the same as the first opinion?' (1) The משנה follows the first speaker in the ברייתא, for whom רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה goes further. (2) The whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה alone, with missing words filled in.
steps.confusionAlert: 'חסורי מחסרא' does not mean the משנה is wrong. It means the משנה is short, and we fill in words to read it properly.

phrases.english: If you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא,
phrases.english: the whole [משנה] is Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka's,
and something is missing
and this is what it teaches:
One who says, 'So-and-so will inherit me'
where there is a daughter;
or 'My daughter will inherit me' where there is a son –
he has said nothing.

phrases.aramaic: הָא בַּת בֵּין הַבָּנוֹת וּבֵן בֵּין הַבָּנִים –
phrases.english: But a daughter among daughters, or a son among sons –
if he said, 'He will inherit all his property,'
his words stand;
for Rabbi Yochanan says:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, called here by his first name only.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר עַל מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לְיוֹרְשׁוֹ –
phrases.english: if he said it about someone fit to inherit him –
his words stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: כּוּלֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה הִיא, וְחַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the problem from Step 5, offered alongside Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the whole משנה as one opinion with missing words filled in.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה has a first opinion and then רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and the two seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole משנה is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. Outsider cases fail, but one son among sons works, because that son is fit to inherit.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, and רבא says the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. רבא also said: the הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling. It follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a father may leave his whole estate to one heir who is fit to inherit him, such as one son among his sons. Two separate rulings, from שמואל (through רב יהודה) and from רבא, agree on this. That makes the ruling especially strong.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows (this opinion)
And so said (another אמורא, agreeing)

steps.whatToRemember: The final law follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. A father may name one fit heir, like one son among his sons, to inherit everything. Naming someone who is not fit to inherit has no effect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for how far a father can change the order of inheritance.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.
And so too Rava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the dispute, the גמרא gives the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה: naming one heir who is fit to inherit, to receive the whole estate, takes effect.

steps.title: רבא gives the verse behind רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה learns his rule from 'ביום הנחילו את בניו': the תורה lets a father leave his estate to whichever heir he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה? The verse says: 'And it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance.' This shows the תורה gave the father permission to give the inheritance to whomever he wants.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we rule like רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, רבא asks where his idea comes from and gives a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on the day HE gives his sons their inheritance' show that the father has a say in how the inheritance is divided. So he may choose one son among sons, or one daughter among daughters, to get everything. This is the source behind the ruling we just saw in Step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason? This asks for the source or logic behind someone's view.
His giving of the inheritance. It comes from נַחֲלָה, inheritance.
Permission. Here, the father's right to choose.

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a תורה basis to the view the גמרא just ruled is the הלכה: a father may choose which fit heir receives his estate.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka?
The verse says:
"And it shall be, on the day he gives his sons their inheritance"
the Torah gave permission to the father
to give the inheritance to whomever he wants.
phrases.notes: He means whomever he wants from among the people who are fit to inherit, as in Step 10.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ruling in Step 11, the גמרא looks for the source of the view it ruled like.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה learns from 'ביום הנחילו את בניו' that a father may give his inheritance to whichever fit heir he chooses.

steps.title: אביי says the rule already comes from 'He may not make firstborn'
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that the father's right to choose among heirs is already learned from 'לא יוכל לבכר', so 'ביום הנחילו' is not needed as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But this rule comes from 'He may not make the son of the beloved wife the firstborn'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's source. He says the same rule is already learned from a different part of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a father may not move the בכור's double portion to another son. The point is that only the בכור's special share is protected, which suggests the father may change how his other sons inherit. If that already teaches the father's right to choose, then 'ביום הנחילו' cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: To make someone the firstborn, giving him the בְּכוֹר's double share.
It comes out from. It means the rule is learned from that source.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי agrees with the rule itself. He is only arguing about which words of the פסוק it comes from.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
This already comes from "He may not make firstborn"!
phrases.notes: This is the rest of the same פסוק, דברים 21:16. Only the firstborn's share is protected, so the father may change things for the other sons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's choice of פסוק from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that 'ביום הנחילו' is the source for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeated source: 'לא יוכל לבכר' already implies the father may change the shares of his other heirs, so a second source is not needed.

steps.title: That verse is needed for a different teaching from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'לא יוכל לבכר' is used for a different lesson, taught in a ברייתא by אבא חנן in the name of רבי אליעזר. The ברייתא itself comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: אבא חנן said in the name of רבי אליעזר:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by saying 'לא יוכל לבכר' teaches something else. This line sets up the ברייתא, and its actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'לא יוכל לבכר' is needed for its own lesson, it is not free to teach the father's right to choose. That leaves 'ביום הנחילו' as the source, just as רבא said. What the other lesson is will only become clear once we hear אבא חנן's words.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for him. The words are being used for a different lesson.
As was taught in a ברייתא.
In the name of. It passes on a teaching from an earlier rabbi.

phrases.english: That phrase is needed for what was taught in a baraita,

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּא חָנָן אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר:
phrases.english: Abba Chanan said in the name of Rabbi Eliezer:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Step 13 by giving 'לא יוכל לבכר' a different job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The other source is needed for a different lesson, so it cannot teach this rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'לא יוכל לבכר' already teaches that the father may choose among his heirs, so 'ביום הנחילו' is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לא יוכל לבכר' is used for אבא חנן's teaching in the ברייתא, so 'ביום הנחילו' remains the source for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
